value.name: Miles addresses young associates
value.description: Miles speaks before the young associates in the conference room, taking the floor to make a personal appeal.
evidence: Miles is addressing the young associates.

value.name: Miles declares vulnerability and love
value.description: Miles announces that he is naked, vulnerable, and in love, revealing a major emotional shift.
evidence: For the first time in my life, I stand before you naked... vulnerable... and in love.

value.name: Miles embraces love openly
value.description: Miles insists that love is not something to fear or be ashamed of, reframing it as a positive force.
evidence: Love. A word matrimonial lawyers shy away from.
I have been frightened of this emotion
Love should cause us no fear. Love should cause us no shame. Love... is good.

value.name: Miles contrasts cynicism with compassion
value.description: Miles argues that lawyers should not exploit clients' heartbreak but instead help revive their love.
evidence: When our clients come to us confused, angry, hurting because their flame of love is fluttering and threatens to die -- should we seek to extinguish that flame, so that we can sift through the smoldering wreckage for our paltry reward?
Or should we seek to fan this precious flame -- this most precious flame -- back to loving, roaring life?

value.name: Miles urges associates to choose love
value.description: Miles delivers a direct moral challenge to the associates, urging them to support love and trust over cynical self-interest.
evidence: Let me ask you a question.
should we seek to extinguish that flame
Or should we seek to fan this precious flame -- this most precious flame -- back to loving, roaring life?
